animations.title: Andromeda–Milky Way Encounter
animations.description: A time-evolving restricted N-body model of a merger-compatible Local Group encounter. Two softened galactic potentials respond to mutual gravity and momentum-conserving orbital drag while massless stellar tracers form bridges, shells and tidal tails.

physics.gravity: two mutually interacting softened point-mass halo potentials
physics.scenario: accelerated merger-compatible realization beginning in the pre-encounter phase
physics.caveat: This is an educational restricted N-body model, not a precision forecast. Current observations allow both merger and non-merger outcomes. Gas, star formation, halo substructure, M33 and the LMC are not resolved here.

references.title: No certainty of a Milky Way–Andromeda collision
The collision between the Milky Way and Andromeda

animations.title: Binary Star Resonance
animations.description: A Newtonian two-body orbit in barycentric coordinates. Kepler's equation is solved each frame for an unequal-mass eccentric binary, while colour and halo size remain artistic audio responses.
animations.equation: M = E - e sin(E); x = a(cos(E)-e); y = a√(1-e²)sin(E)
animations.numerics: Eight Newton iterations per frame; G = 1, m₁ = 1.2, m₂ = 0.8, a = 1.45, e = 0.34

physics.model: Newtonian two-body Kepler orbit in barycentric coordinates
physics.method: Kepler equation solved by Newton iteration
physics.caveat: The orbit is an ideal isolated two-body model. Stellar structure, tides, mass transfer and relativistic effects are omitted; audio changes only halo scale and colour response.

references.title: NASA GSFC: Kepler's Laws of Orbital Motion
